messages:
Liam K: hi folks, day 1 stuck — can't curl http://10.12.5.20 (internal dashboard) from WSL2 while on Cloudflare WARP split-tunnel. host (Windows) can reach it.
Rhea T: welcome! can you curl from Windows cmd/powershell and from inside WSL? what VPN client settings do you have?
Liam K: Powershell: curl http://10.12.5.20 -> 200 OK. WSL: curl -> Connection timed out. I'm on WARP (Teams) in split-tunnel mode, allowed apps only.
IT Ops: common WSL/WARP issue: WARP installs a virtual adapter and Windows routes internal subnets through it, but WSL2 has a separate network namespace and doesn't inherit the Windows route.
Sam M: yep. quick checks: from Windows run `ipconfig /all` and inside WSL `ip route` and `cat /etc/resolv.conf`.
Liam K: Windows shows route for 10.12.0.0/16 via WARP adapter. WSL `ip route` shows default via 172.24.96.1 (vEthernet), no 10.12 route. /etc/resolv.conf points to 172.24.96.1.
Rhea T: options: (1) use SSH proxy via bastion from WSL: `ssh -o ProxyCommand="ssh -W %h:%p liam@bastion.redwood.com" user@10.12.5.20`, (2) add a route inside WSL: `sudo ip route add 10.12.0.0/16 via 172.24.96.1` (temporary), or (3) enable WARP setting to "Allow LAN access" / include 10.12.0.0/16 in routes so WSL traffic is forwarded.
IT Ops: note: adding route in WSL will work until WSL restarts. For a persistent fix, create a small startup script in /etc/wsl.conf to run on boot, or configure Docker/WSL integration to share routes. If using Docker Desktop with WSL backend, also ensure Docker's WSL distro has the route.
Liam K: added `sudo ip route add 10.12.0.0/16 via 172.24.96.1` and now curl works from WSL. thanks!
infra-bot: ticket INF-4999 created to add WSL2 + WARP troubleshooting note to onboarding docs (assigned to eng-infra).
Sam M: we'll add a snippet to the new-hires checklist: "If on Windows+WARP and using WSL2, add route or use bastion proxy."
Liam K: awesome, appreciate the help :tada:
